name: Rapid freezing of fresh frozen plasma in a contact shock freezer (core -30 C within 1 h, freezer at -50 C) and frozen storage at -40 C
plain_name: Quick-freeze donated plasma so its clotting factors survive
description: Blood-bank FFP preparation: plasma bags are frozen in a contact shock freezer operating at -50 C so the core reaches -30 C within 40 min (guideline: within 1 h), then kept stacked in a -40 C deep freezer; AABB requires -18 C or colder.
keywords: Quick-freeze donated plasma so its clotting factors survive

sources.citation: Dhantole L, Dubey A, Sonker A. A study on factors influencing the hemostatic potential of fresh frozen plasma. Asian J Transfus Sci 2019. DOI 10.4103/ajts.AJTS_139_17
Circular of Information for the Use of Human Blood and Blood Components (AABB, American Red Cross, America's Blood Centers, Armed Services Blood Program)

requirements.rationale: Plasma must be brought to a core temperature of -30 C or below, so the freezer must reach -30 C or colder.
Regulatory minimum for FFP: frozen at -18 C or colder.
Operating point used for storage in the study: -40 C deep freezer (any -18 C or colder store meets the AABB rule).
The contact shock freezer used operates at -50 C, which achieved the -30 C core in 40 min.

confirmation_note: Requirements taken from the cited procedure and independently re-verified against the source (research/v4, 2026-11-01). Users must confirm them for their own run; edits require confirmation again.
